L1_casesummary: I am writing regarding the recent notice that Scotiabank intends to terminate my banking relationship and close all of my accounts due to suspected fraudulent activity. I respectfully request that this decision be reviewed and reconsidered  as I believe there has been a misunderstanding regarding the nature of the transactions in my account. I have been a client of Scotiabank since 2019 and have maintained my accounts in good standing. Throughout this time  I have consistently managed my financial obligations responsibly. Even during the current financial challenges I am facing due to an ongoing divorce  I have continued to keep my credit cards and line of credit payments current. Prior to these circumstances  I also made regular contributions to my TFSA and RRSP accounts. In addition  I previously worked with Scotiabank for several years in various roles  including as a Financial Advisor. During my time there  I helped open numerous client accounts and became familiar with the bank’s policies and compliance standards. Because of this experience  I have always been careful to respect and properly use the bank’s products and services. For that reason  it was extremely disheartening to learn that my accounts are being closed without the opportunity to clarify the transactions that appear to have raised concerns. The transactions that may have been flagged as suspicious are actually normal transactions related to assisting my brother’s business operations. My brother owns a grocery business in Winnipeg and holds accounts with both RBC and Scotiabank. His business receives daily deposits into his RBC account. However  when purchasing inventory from vendors  his e-Transfer limits can sometimes prevent him from sending the required payments  and cheque deposits can be subject to holds. Because of this  I occasionally assisted by sending payments from my account on his behalf. The weekly purchase amounts typically range between $4 000 and $8 000 depending on the quantity ordered. These purchases are for Indian jaggery (sugar)  which is a product that customers frequently buy in large quantities from the grocery store. I would be happy to provide invoices or supporting documentation if required to verify the legitimacy of these transactions. Since opening my accounts in 2019  I have only had two cheques returned  and I maintain a strong credit profile. My credit score typically ranges between 730 and 770. My financial history reflects responsible account managemen

L2_casesummary: The customer reports having contacted the mortgage helpline multiple times over the years to postpone mortgage payments due to their spouse’s sick leave. No reporting errors to credit bureaus were identified and no corrections were deemed necessary.Regarding the customer’s concern about duplicate withdrawals and NSF fees the bank confirmed that a scheduled payment in November 2024 was not processed resulting in insufficient‑funds fees. These fees were subsequently reversed on December 24 2024.

Upon attending the branch on March 24 they were advised that interest rates had increased to 4.1% and were informed for the first time that the previously quoted rate had expired the day prior. The clients stated that no disclosure was provided at any point that the quoted rate was timelimited nor was an apology or accountability offered at the time. They indicated that had they been informed of an expiration they would have attended earlier. When they declined to proceed at the higher rate the advisor indicated an exception request would be submitted.Nearly a week later the clients received a written apology and were advised that efforts were being made to secure the original 3.77% online rate. The client is requesting that the verbally accepted rate of 3.73% provided by the advisor be honoured.

Client nous confirme également qu'il n'a pas donné d'instructions comme quoi il voulait que le prêt se renouvelle ouvert (aucune conversation téléphonique  aucun courriel). Il ne s'agit pas de la faute de la Banque Scotia s'il y a eu des délais supplémentaires dans son dossier avec sa nouvelle institution. De plus  comme il n'y a pas eu d'erreur de notre côté dans le traitement et étant donné que le client n'a pas d'autres produits avec nous  la succursale n'est pas en mesure de justifier un montant en dédommagement.

L1_casesummary: Demande de crédit a débuté avec le client le 5 décembre 2024. Client avait pour projet de consolider dettes BMO et Scotia. Lors du rendez-vous  j'ai fait un calcul du ratio d'endettement du client avec différents scénarios afin de déterminer ce qui serait possible de faire. Le client m'a donc fait part verbalement de ses dettes externes afin d'effectuer le calcul. Il a omis de me mentionner une location de véhicule avec VolksWagen  car il croyait qu'il était question uniquement de ses cartes et lignes de crédit. La situation financière du client est devenue précaire récemment en raison d'un changement d'emploi. Il gagnait considérablement plus à son emploi précédent. Il l'a quitté puisque l'environnement était toxique et craignait pour sa santé mentale.
L1_resolutionsummary: J'ai expliqué au client les 3 éléments que la Banque considère lors d'une demande hypothécaire: 1) Est-ce que la valeur de la propriété supporte la demande? 2) Est-ce que le bureau de crédit est satisfaisant? 3) Est-ce que le ratio d'endettement permet de supporter la demande? . Dans la situation présente  les points 1 et 2 sont remplis  mais le ratio d'endettement ne permet pas d'aller de l'avant en raison de la location VW. Bien qu'il reste moins de $3 000.00 à la location  le montant de rachat du véhicule est d'environ $21 000.00. Sans la dette VW  nous pourrions financer un CIS de $257 400.00  ce qui serait suffisant pour consolider les dettes. J'ai proposé au client d'attendre au moins d'avril pour que sa location soit terminée ou bien qu'il règle le tout avant. Client n'est pas satisfait. J'ai également escaladé la situation à ACE. La réponse reçue de la part de ACE laisse croire qu'ils ont également regarder une façon de faire fonctionner le financement. La seule solution est de diminuer le montant à emprunter  mais il ne serait pas possible de consolider les dettes avec un montant moindre. J'ai avisé que la situation serait escaladée afin de ne pas oublier d'éléments. Svp  proposer au client de bien s'entourer et de chercher de l'aide psychologique advenant un refus définitif  il est actuellement fragile psychologiquement.
